content.comment_body: Hi [user_name], I want to know if it's possible to change the counter value between two [product_name] devices without using the [product_name] Access Tool. Is there another way to transfer values between [product_name]? I managed to do this via network analog output, but the value stays at 32767. I need to count up to 500000. The program is attached.

You can read the counter value (up to 999,999) and transfer it via VM parameter mapping from one [product_name] to another, without using the Access Tool. However, on the receiving [product_name], there's no way to display the value. Could you clarify what you want to achieve with the counter value on the second [product_name]?

This setup is for an agricultural machine that plants seeds in the ground. It has 8 units, each dropping 20 seeds per second. The main goal is to monitor the seed count and prevent issues. Two [product_name] devices are used for fast counting, and I need to know the number of seeds planted by the end of the day.

Are the two [product_name]s located in different places, or do you not have displays? As mentioned, you can transfer a counter value (up to 999,999) to another [product_name], but you can't display or further process the value on the second device. The mathematical limits for [product_name] are -32,768 and 32,767 due to integer value restrictions.

Hi [user_name], thank you for your assistance. I have displays and two [product_name]s working together. The entire machine is controlled from a single display, with one [product_name] dedicated only for fast counting.

I performed another test. Initially, I ruled out this option because it didn't work in simulation. When I tested with two actual [product_name]s, it worked. You can transfer a counter value higher than 32,767 (up to 999,999) to another [product_name], and display it using another counter.

Dear [user_name], thank you for your solution. I tried your suggestion and it worked well, but I couldn't replicate it at my workplace. I think I made a mistake—B005 ... B008 aren't working. Can you assist me?
You also need to transfer the V-words (VW0, VW4, VW8, and VW12) to the other [product_name]. I’ve set it up for you; see the attached file.
Thank you very much for your help. This solution was extremely useful to me.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced difficulties transferring large counter values between two [product_name] devices due to integer limitations and display restrictions. Joint troubleshooting clarified successful methods for transferring and displaying higher counter values, leading to improved usage and clearer results.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to transfer and display counter values exceeding 32,767 between two [product_name] devices without relying on extra software, enabling accurate monitoring of machine performance.
